'''Niklaus J. Grünwald''' is a [[biologist]] and [[plant pathologist]] born and raised in [[Caracas, Venezuela]] of German and Swiss ancestry. He is currently a research scientist with the USDA [[Agricultural Research Service]], a Professor (Courtesy) in the Department of Botany and Plant Pathology at [[Oregon State University]], and a Professor (Adjunct) in the Department of Plant Pathology and Plant-Microbe Biology at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web
| url          = http://www.apsnet.org/members/awards/RuthAllen/Pages/NiklausJGr%C3%BCnwald.aspx
| title        = Biographical Sketch
| date         = 2015
| website      = 
| publisher    = American Phytopathological Society

| archive-date = 2016-04-23
| quote        = 
}}</ref>

==Education==
Grünwald obtained a BSc in [[plant science]] at [[University of California, Davis]] ([[UC Davis]]) in 1992. He completed his PhD in [[ecology]] and [[plant pathology]] in 1997 at [[UC Davis]] studying the effect of cover crop decomposition on soil nutrient cycling and soil microbiology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://harvest.lib.ucdavis.edu/F/?func=direct&doc_number=000525166&local_base=UCD01PUB |title=Pds Sso |publisher=Harvest.lib.ucdavis.edu |date= |access-date=2015-08-31}}</ref><ref name="bio" /> He pursued postdoctoral research at Cornell University.

==Research==
His academic research<ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|t55Dt5sAAAAJ}}</ref> focuses on the [[evolution]], [[genomics]], and [[ecology]] of plant pathogens in the genus ''[[Phytophthora]]'' and management of the diseases they cause. L. | issue = 1| pmid = 16356717}}</ref> Grünwald is best known for providing novel insights into how plant pathogens emerge, methods to study pathogen evolution, particularly when populations are clonal, and characterizing the evolutionary history of ''Phytophthora'' pathogens. In collaboration with one of his students he developed the concept of heat trees to show differential abundance of species (or other hierarchical data like gene expression) in a tree format.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Foster |first1=Zachary S. L. |last2=Sharpton |first2=Thomas J. |last3=Grünwald |first3=Niklaus J. |last4=Poisot |first4=Timothée |title=Metacoder: An R package for visualization and manipulation of community taxonomic diversity data |journal=PLOS Computational Biology |date=21 February 2017 |volume=13 |issue=2 |article-number=e1005404 |doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005404|pmc=5340466 |pmid=28222096 |bibcode=2017PLSCB..13E5404F |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Honors and awards==

* 1991 [[Phi Kappa Phi]]
* 1992 Summa Cum Laude, [[UC Davis]]
* 1992 Outstanding undergraduate performance, Agricultural Science and Management [[UC Davis]]
* 1996 [[Sigma Xi]]
* 2006 USDA ARS Early Career Award<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ars.usda.gov/news-events/news/research-news/2007/ars-honors-top-scientists-for-2006/ |title=ARS |publisher=Ars.usda.gov |date= |access-date=2015-08-31}}</ref>
* 2007 Syngenta Award,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.apsnet.org/members/awards/Syngenta/Pages/NiklausJGr%C3%BCnwald.aspx |title=Niklaus J. Grünwald |publisher=Apsnet.org |date= |access-date=2015-08-31}}</ref> [[American Phytopathological Society]]
* 2015 Ruth Allen Award,<ref name="bio"/> [[American Phytopathological Society]]. This award is named after the first female plant pathologist, [[Ruth F. Allen]], and given for outstanding, innovative research contribution that has changed, or has the potential to change, the direction of research in any field of plant pathology.
